---
title: "Hazard data"
---
FIAT computes the impact of a flood event or the risk of flooding on a community by using flood maps as hazard input. Flood maps describe the potential flood extent and magnitude in specific geographic areas. Currently, FIAT is only

These flood maps can be obtained from various sources. The [The Global Flood Database](http://global-flood-database.cloudtostreet.info/) provides an extensive amount of global flood hazard mapping products.

::: {.callout-tip}
The user can also create their own flood model using the [**SFINCS model**](https://sfincs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html)
:::

The user is free to run the model with a variety of flood scenarios, e.g., including mitigation and adaptation measures over a range of future climate conditions, as long as flood maps are available for those scenarios. The flood maps can be either **flood elevation** or **flood depth** maps.


::: {.callout-caution}
**Flood elevation maps** use the **datum** as a reference point, whereas **flood depth maps** use the **ground elevation** to refer to. The datum of the elevation map must be the same as the one used to obtain the ground elevation in the exposure data.
:::

With FIAT, the user has the option to assess the impact of a single flood event or the flood risk based on a set of events with multiple return periods. To do the latter, the user must provide multiple hazard maps with the same extent and projection.

In each case, some requirements must be met. The hazard files of any map should be made available as a **raster file**, see the acceptable file types at the bottom of this page. It is recommended to place the hazard files in the 'hazard' directory, see the [directory structure](index.qmd#directory-structure). The file name is free to be chosen by the user and must simply be refered to in the [settings.toml](../settings/index.qmd) configuration file.

## Types of maps
FIAT knows two types of hazard maps:

- [Event maps](hazard_maps.qmd#event)
- [Risk maps](hazard_maps.qmd#risk)

Risk maps are mainly used to calculate the EAD (Estimated Annual Damages).
If `risk` is not set to `true` in the [settings file](../settings/index.qmd), the supplied map will be treated as an event map.

## Hazard types
Every band (variable) of the hazard file has a hazard **type**, set with a `type` attribute on the band, e.g.:

- `water_depth`: flood depth;
- `water_level`: flood elevation (level), only for geometry exposure (method `flood.level`);
- `flood_duration`: flood duration.

The [methods](vulnerability.qmd#methods) of the linked vulnerability datasets determine which types are needed. A hazard file can therefore hold bands of several types, e.g. a `depth` band and a `duration` band for the method `flood.depth_duration`. In case of a risk calculation, every return period must have a band of every needed type; the return period of a band is set with an `rp` attribute (see [risk maps](hazard_maps.qmd#return-periods)).

## Settings
The type and return period of a band can also be set (or overridden) in the [settings file](../settings/index.qmd) with a `[[hazard.variables]]` entry per band. A setting in the settings file takes precedence over the attribute in the file.

```toml
[hazard]
file = "risk_map.nc"

[[hazard.variables]]
name = "depth_rp10"
type = "water_depth"                      # overrides the 'type' attribute
rp = 10                                   # overrides the 'rp' attribute

[[hazard.variables]]
name = "duration_rp10"                    # not in the file: uniform layer
type = "flood_duration"
rp = 10
value = 3.0
```

- `name`: the name of the band (variable); it must exist in the file, unless `value` is set.
- `type`: the hazard type of the band.
- `rp`: the return period of the band (risk calculations).
- `value`: a constant value, see [uniform layers](#uniform-layers).

### Uniform layers
A `[[hazard.variables]]` entry with a `value` defines a uniform layer: a band that is not in the file and has the same (constant) value over the whole grid, e.g. a flood duration of 3 days. The `name` must be a **new** variable (not present in the file) and the entry must have a `type`, as there are no attributes in the file to fall back on. Otherwise FIAT stops with an error when reading the hazard data.
